chunks: My group of scholars narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Uqbah ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I visit the mosques around the city; which one should I start with?' He said: 'Start with Quba and pray in it, and increase [your prayers], for it is the first mosque in this area in which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed. Then go to the Well of Umm Ibrahim and pray in it, for that is the dwelling place of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his place of prayer. Then you go to the Mosque of Fadikh and pray two Rak'ah in it, for your Prophet has prayed in it. When you have finished this side, go to the side of Uhud. Start with the mosque that is below the Harrah, and when you have prayed in it, then pass by the grave of Hamzah, and the hadith is long.'

key_terms.جَانِبَ أُحُدٍ: The side of Uhud, referring to the area near the Mount of Uhud
key_terms.قَبْرَ حَمْزَةَ: The grave of Hamzah, the uncle of the Prophet
key_terms.قُبَا: Mosque of Quba, the first mosque built by the Prophet in Medina
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ الْفَضِيخِ: Mosque of Fadikh, a specific mosque in Medina
key_terms.مَشْرَبَةَ أُمِّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The Well of Umm Ibrahim, associated with the Prophet's residence

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended order for visiting mosques in Medina according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a specific ritual itinerary for pilgrims, emphasizing the historical precedence of the Prophet’s (saw) personal worship spaces over mere architectural grandeur. By prioritizing the Mosque of Quba as the first mosque and linking the Well of Umm Ibrahim to the Prophet’s residence, the text underscores the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarat* as a means of connecting with the lived reality and spiritual legacy of the Ahl al-Bayt. The sequence reflects a structured approach to sanctifying time and space through repeated prayer at sites of prophetic significance.
